# Bundled Clay

Upstream revision: `e6cc36941ab2af5d81107617039d6f527a1c660b`.
Original header SHA256: `54aef6d5f96b14e296bebb6db4a755543e98fd7e6c188411afb2f22a4b4f7728`.
The unchanged original is also kept at `tests/clay/vendor/clay.h` for the historical standalone proofs. The license remains in `licenses/LICENSE.clay`.

`clay-local.patch` records the complete header difference from that pin. It must reconstruct `third_party/clay.h` from the original header; update it in the same commit as each header change. The production solver tests compile this same header.

The first extension is `Clay__OpenTextElementWithLayout`: an explicit stable element ID and optional `Clay_TextElementLayout` let word-wrapped text own a FIT/GROW allocation and vertically align its glyph commands. Horizontal alignment remains the existing text configuration. The original `CLAY_TEXT` entry point keeps its implicit ID and intrinsic text behavior. Fixed/percent sizes, bounds, padding, paint, clipping and floating text areas continue to use real container elements in the widget compiler.

The optional layout is stored beside the text payload inside `Clay_LayoutElement`'s union. It must never be written through the container `config` member, which aliases font, paint, owner and text data. Sizing uses the existing axis stages; wrapping retains natural line widths; the existing command stage applies vertical alignment within the allocated text area. No additional layout pass, geometry feedback, renderer placement calculation or off-tree painter is introduced.

Validation covers stable IDs, actual text areas and pointer hits outside glyphs, native attachments, glyph rectangles/font/color/owner data, existing primitive behavior, real-font pixel comparisons, original Lua input and lookup, retained sizing boundaries, and bundled compositor regressions.

`Clay_ClipElementConfig.passive` clips overflowing content using the existing axis and command stages, with authored `childOffset`, without allocating or accepting scrolling state. Switching an existing scrolling element to passive retires its state. The default remains an ordinary scrolling clip. The new flag occupies existing padding in the clip config. Definite widget hosts use passive clips so their growing content retains overflow without a floating root or a previous-drawable-size minimum. FIT popup roots keep ordinary compressible content sizing. Native tests cover clipped input, offsets, overflow, state retirement and 120 passive roots alongside an ordinary scroll container.

`Clay_LayoutConfig.ceilGrow` preserves fair layout's whole-pixel allocation policy inside the existing axis-sizing stage: leading GROW children round upward, and the final GROW child retains the remainder without dropping its minimum. Authored sizing and ordinary default allocation are unchanged; FIXED/PERCENT/FIT children and floating sizing do not use this rounding. Bounds remain bounds, and the inspector exposes the selected policy. Fair's Lua producer supplies grouping and policy only, with no sibling rectangles or geometry feedback.

`Clay_LayoutConfig.sizeContain` represents an independently allocated container whose children keep their own sizing and may overhang. Its intrinsic size comes from its own padding and declared bounds, and child wrapping does not enlarge that intrinsic size. This affects the existing close/height-propagation stages only; child layout, paint, input and attachment traversal remain ordinary native behavior, without clipping or another solve. Fair client frames use it so protocol surface minima do not change their assigned cells. The inspector shows the containment policy.

`Clay_AspectRatioElementConfig.sourceDimensions` supplies an image's natural width and height beside its aspect ratio. Zero source dimensions keep the original upstream aspect path. Source dimensions seed preferred content during close without becoming minima. The normal horizontal sizing stage measures image-bearing content from current definite constraints before counting FIT ancestors, then the existing horizontal and vertical allocation stages constrain the aspect image. Per-solve limits stay separate from authored min/max declarations. Floating roots retain their already assigned allocations. No previous host rectangle, auxiliary Clay layout or frame convergence supplies image sizing. The traversal visits each image-bearing subtree once per normal solve; non-image subtrees are skipped. Built-in imagebox and tray producers and supported ad-hoc image declarations use this same native path. Distinct image and widget allocations retain their containers and bindings.

Intrinsic aspect images retain the producers' outward whole-pixel rounding on both fitted axes. The natural source ratio is evaluated in double precision when it agrees with the declared ratio, avoiding a float approximation turning an exact 2:7 image at height 21 into a 7px width. Explicit fixed axes remain authored. Native tests and base/current pixel captures cover landscape and portrait ratios, including fractional widths.

Final root positioning and command generation traverse roots in declaration order, so a nested floating shadow below its owner's zIndex reads the owner's current box on first open, movement and FIT resizing. Each root retains its declaration ordinal across the existing transition/debug traversals. The unchanged upstream stable zIndex sort then orders the roots, and each root's contiguous balanced command range moves with it using arena scratch storage. Pointer state and debug consumers still see the sorted roots and command stream; equal-band order, scissor scopes, transitions and culling keep their existing rules. This changes no compositor geometry and introduces no additional solve. Production-solver regressions cover lower-band first-open/move/FIT grow/shrink/in-flow ownership, equal-band order, higher-band nesting, sorted pointer traversal and balanced scissor ranges.

`Clay_ElementDeclaration.backgroundBeforeRoots` declares OUTPUT's unclipped backdrop. The existing command ordering stage places that element's own color/image before all roots; its in-flow children retain band 0, above negative-band desktop objects. No floating element, background record, band, layout pass or renderer placement writer supplies the backdrop. For this property, `backgroundColor` paints beneath an image instead of tinting it, preserving filtered image edges and transparent pixels. Other image declarations retain their existing tint semantics. This property is used only on the un-clipped OUTPUT element, outside overlay/scissor scopes. Root command ranges describe their remaining balanced commands after backdrop extraction. Native tests cover color, image, combined underlay/image, negative-band overlap, flow children, repeated frames and transition traversal. The historical vendor header remains unchanged.

`Clay_ClipElementConfig.toPadding` and optional clip-command `userData` support decorated host contributions. The existing clip command and pointer stages use the padded content rectangle; attached children inherit the same rectangle. The host's border is emitted after this scissor closes, with its own unchanged metadata. A separate clip word lets the renderer retain the content scope without applying content opacity or input ownership to the border. Ordinary clips keep their previous border order and metadata. Hosts use this with `passive`, without adding scroll state, layout passes or geometry feedback. Rounded content retains its separate mask boundary. The native inspector exposes the padding policy. Production solver tests cover flow and floating clipping, pointer rejection in padding, resize, border ordering, independent metadata and zero scroll-state allocation; headful border/decor/input fixtures exercise the actual renderer.
